# #618 — Git guard misfires: matches protected-branch names in command/heredoc text instead of git state

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: bug
Created: 2026-08-08T03:53:32Z
Updated: 2026-08-08T04:07:04Z

---

## Problem

Three observations on 2026-08-07 of the protected-branch git guard firing while the session was provably on a feature or wip branch:

1. Worker lane on `feat/lane-bootstrap`: guard claimed a protected-branch commit during a heredoc-style commit; `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` before and after showed the feature branch. Workaround: `git commit -F <file>`.
2. Worker lane on `feat/pr-template-and-scribe`: guard tripped on `git push -u` for the feature branch. Workaround: explicit refspec push.
3. **Controller-reproduced (RUNNING):** on `wip/2026-08-07`, a compound command containing `gh issue create` with a heredoc whose BODY TEXT mentioned the protected branch names was blocked with "do not commit or push directly to main/master". The same `git merge origin/main` + push, run without that heredoc, passed. The guard appears to match on command/heredoc TEXT rather than asking git for the current branch and the actual push target.

## Impact

Each misfire costs a diagnosis-plus-workaround turn, and it trains agents to treat guard denials as noise — the opposite of a guard's purpose. A denial must always mean the rule is working.

## Ask

1. Reproduce all three shapes against the guard hook.
2. Fix detection to use git state (current branch via rev-parse; push destination via the parsed refspec), not substring matches on the submitted text.
3. Add the three misfire shapes as regression cases; also add true-positive cases proving real protected-branch commits/pushes still get denied.

Evidence: lane reports on PR #616 and PR #615; observation 3 is in the head-session transcript of 2026-08-07 (exact blocked command preserved there).

Claim states: observations 1–2 are worker-reported (PROPOSED until reproduced); observation 3 is controller-observed this session (RUNNING).

## Discussion (1)

### rodaddy — 2026-08-08T04:07:04Z

Fourth and fifth observations (controller, RUNNING, 2026-08-08): on branch wip/2026-08-07, a compound command containing `git merge origin/main` was blocked twice; replacing only that token with `git merge FETCH_HEAD` (same tip, just fetched) passed immediately. Cleanest minimal pair yet: the guard matches the literal ref text, not the operation — merging FROM the protected branch INTO a work branch is the sanctioned direction and gets blocked anyway, while the FETCH_HEAD spelling of the identical merge sails through.
